header: Inspired by publicly described methods. Not affiliated with, endorsed by, or representing the people named. Educational tool, not investment advice.
note: Each card describes a published method and an approximation of it as a screen. It is not a ranking of the method, the screen or any symbol.

cards.name: Minervini-style trend template

who.text: US stock trader who set out his approach in the 2013 book Trade Like a Stock Market Wizard.

style.text: Trend following in stocks: a stock qualifies only when a checklist of price and moving-average conditions shows a long-term uptrend.

looks_for.text: Price above the 50, 150 and 200-day averages in that order, a rising 200-day, near the 52-week high, well off the low, high relative strength.

timeframe.text: Daily bars; a trend filter applied before looking for a base and a breakout.

cards.source_line: Source: Trade Like a Stock Market Wizard: How to Achieve Super Performance in Stocks in Any Market (2013), Mark Minervini

sources.title: Trade Like a Stock Market Wizard: How to Achieve Super Performance in Stocks in Any Market
sources.covers: The trend template: price and moving-average order (50, 150, 200-day), a rising 200-day average, distance from the 52-week high and low, and a relative-strength ranking.
sources.citation: Trade Like a Stock Market Wizard: How to Achieve Super Performance in Stocks in Any Market (2013), Mark Minervini

cards.approximation: Relative strength here is the percentile of the 250-bar % change within the scanned list, not a published rating; 52 weeks = 250 bars; rising = above its value 21 bars ago.
cards.disclaimer: Inspired by publicly described methods. Not affiliated with, endorsed by, or representing Mark Minervini. Educational tool, not investment advice.

screen.source: close > SMA(close, 50) AND SMA(close, 50) > SMA(close, 150) AND SMA(close, 150) > SMA(close, 200) AND SMA(close, 200) > SMA(close, 200)[21] AND close >= $near_high * Max(high, 250) AND close >= $above_low * Min(low, 250) AND PercentileRank(PctChange(close, 250)) >= $rs_min

params.name: near_high
params.doc: Close at least this fraction of the 52-week high (0.75 = within 25% of it).

params.name: above_low
params.doc: Close at least this multiple of the 52-week low (1.3 = 30% above it).

params.name: rs_min
params.doc: Lowest relative-strength percentile within the scanned list.

cards.name: Darvas-style box breakout

who.text: Professional dancer who described the stock-trading method he used in a 1960 book.

style.text: Box theory: a rising stock moves through a series of price boxes; he acted only when price rose out of the top of the latest box.

looks_for.text: A close above a tight consolidation (the box) to a new high for the period, on volume above its recent average, near the 52-week high.

timeframe.text: Daily bars; positions held while price keeps forming higher boxes.

cards.source_line: Source: How I Made $2,000,000 in the Stock Market (1960), Nicolas Darvas

sources.title: How I Made $2,000,000 in the Stock Market
sources.covers: The box theory: rising stocks moving through a series of price boxes, action only when price leaves the top of the latest box, attention to volume, and the author's background as a professional dancer.
sources.citation: How I Made $2,000,000 in the Stock Market (1960), Nicolas Darvas

cards.approximation: The box here is the high and low of the previous 20 bars, at most 15% deep; the book draws its boxes by eye from daily highs and lows.
cards.disclaimer: Inspired by publicly described methods. Not affiliated with, endorsed by, or representing Nicolas Darvas. Educational tool, not investment advice.

screen.source: close > Max(high, $box_bars)[1] AND Min(low, $box_bars)[1] >= $box_floor * Max(high, $box_bars)[1] AND volume >= $vol_mult * SMA(volume, 50)[1] AND close >= $near_high * Max(high, 250)

params.name: box_bars
params.doc: Bars that make up the box before today.

params.name: box_floor
params.doc: Box low at least this fraction of the box high (0.85 = at most 15% deep).

params.name: vol_mult
params.doc: Volume at least this multiple of its 50-bar average.

params.name: near_high
params.doc: Close at least this fraction of the 52-week high.

cards.name: Weinstein-style stage 2 breakout

who.text: Technical analyst who described stage analysis in a 1988 book on bull and bear markets.

style.text: Stage analysis: a stock moves through four stages (base, advance, top, decline), read on the weekly chart and its 30-week moving average.

looks_for.text: A weekly close above the prior base high and above a flat or rising 30-week average, on volume well above its recent average.

timeframe.text: Weekly bars; positional holding periods of months.

cards.source_line: Source: Stan Weinstein's Secrets for Profiting in Bull and Bear Markets (1988), Stan Weinstein

sources.title: Stan Weinstein's Secrets for Profiting in Bull and Bear Markets
sources.covers: Stage analysis on weekly charts: four stages (basing, advancing, top, declining), the 30-week moving average, the stage 2 breakout above resistance with expanding volume, and relative strength.
sources.citation: Stan Weinstein's Secrets for Profiting in Bull and Bear Markets (1988), Stan Weinstein

cards.approximation: The base here is the high of the previous 10 weeks; flat or rising = the 30-week average not below its value 1 and 4 weeks ago; volume vs the 4 weeks before; no relative-strength check yet.
cards.disclaimer: Inspired by publicly described methods. Not affiliated with, endorsed by, or representing Stan Weinstein. Educational tool, not investment advice.

screen.source: close > SMA(close, 30) AND SMA(close, 30) >= SMA(close, 30)[1] AND SMA(close, 30) >= SMA(close, 30)[4] AND close > Max(high, $base_weeks)[1] AND volume >= $vol_mult * SMA(volume, 4)[1]

params.name: base_weeks
params.doc: Weeks of base before this week.

params.name: vol_mult
params.doc: Weekly volume at least this multiple of the 4 weeks before.

cards.legend: Richard Dennis, William Eckhardt and the Turtle traders
cards.name: Turtle-style 20-day channel breakout

who.text: Traders trained in the 1980s by Richard Dennis and William Eckhardt; former Turtles later published the rules.

style.text: Systematic trend following: entries on channel breakouts, with position size and stops set from volatility (N, an average true range).

looks_for.text: The day's high above the highest high of the previous 20 days (System 1); System 2 used 55 days.

timeframe.text: Daily bars; trades lasting days to months; the rules were written for futures markets.

cards.source_line: Source: Way of the Turtle: The Secret Methods that Turned Ordinary People into Legendary Traders (2007), Curtis M. Faith; The Complete TurtleTrader: The Legend, the Lessons, the Results (2007), Michael W. Covel

sources.title: Way of the Turtle: The Secret Methods that Turned Ordinary People into Legendary Traders
sources.covers: The Turtle program run by Richard Dennis and William Eckhardt, and its rules: channel breakouts of 20 days (System 1) and 55 days (System 2), volatility (N, an average true range) for position size and stops, futures markets.
sources.citation: Way of the Turtle: The Secret Methods that Turned Ordinary People into Legendary Traders (2007), Curtis M. Faith

sources.title: The Complete TurtleTrader: The Legend, the Lessons, the Results
sources.covers: The history of the Turtle program (Richard Dennis, William Eckhardt, the traders they trained in the 1980s) and its breakout rules.
sources.citation: The Complete TurtleTrader: The Legend, the Lessons, the Results (2007), Michael W. Covel

cards.approximation: Long side only here (the rules were symmetric); System 1's filter that skips a breakout after a winning one is not included.
cards.disclaimer: Inspired by publicly described methods. Not affiliated with, endorsed by, or representing Richard Dennis, William Eckhardt and the Turtle traders. Educational tool, not investment advice.

params.name: entry_days
params.doc: Channel length in days (20 = System 1, 55 = System 2).

cards.legend: Linda Bradford Raschke and Laurence Connors
cards.name: Raschke-style ADX pullback to the 20 EMA

who.text: Futures trader; co-author with Laurence Connors of the 1995 book Street Smarts.

style.text: Short-term pullbacks in strong trends, with the ADX used to judge trend strength.

looks_for.text: ADX(14) above 30 and a pullback whose low touches the 20-period EMA after trading above it; the trigger is a move above the pullback bar's high.

timeframe.text: Daily bars; a short-term setup lasting days.

cards.source_line: Source: Street Smarts: High Probability Short-Term Trading Strategies (1995), Laurence A. Connors and Linda Bradford Raschke

sources.title: Street Smarts: High Probability Short-Term Trading Strategies
sources.covers: Short-term setups, including the ADX pullback to the 20-period exponential moving average (14-period ADX above 30 marking a strong trend, entry trigger above the high of the pullback bar).
sources.citation: Street Smarts: High Probability Short-Term Trading Strategies (1995), Laurence A. Connors and Linda Bradford Raschke

cards.approximation: An uptrend here is a 20-period EMA above its value 5 bars ago; ADX rising beforehand is not checked; long side only; the screen lists the touch, and the trigger bar is left for the trader to watch.
cards.disclaimer: Inspired by publicly described methods. Not affiliated with, endorsed by, or representing Linda Bradford Raschke and Laurence Connors. Educational tool, not investment advice.

screen.source: ADX(14) > $adx_min AND EMA(close, 20) > EMA(close, 20)[5] AND low <= EMA(close, 20) AND low[1] > EMA(close, 20)[1]

params.name: adx_min
params.doc: Lowest ADX(14) reading that counts as a strong trend.

cards.name: Crabel-style NR7 range contraction

who.text: Trader and author of a 1990 statistical study of short-term price patterns and the opening-range breakout.

style.text: Short-term patterns studied statistically, such as range contraction and breakouts from the opening range.

looks_for.text: An NR7 day: today's high-low range is narrower than that of each of the previous six days (range contraction).

timeframe.text: Daily bars; the follow-through is studied over the next session.

cards.source_line: Source: Day Trading with Short Term Price Patterns and Opening Range Breakout (1990), Toby Crabel

sources.title: Day Trading with Short Term Price Patterns and Opening Range Breakout
sources.covers: Statistical study of short-term price patterns: range contraction (narrow-range days such as NR4 and NR7, inside days) and the opening-range breakout.
sources.citation: Day Trading with Short Term Price Patterns and Opening Range Breakout (1990), Toby Crabel

cards.approximation: The screen lists NR7 days in either direction; the opening-range breakout that follows needs intraday bars and is not part of it.
cards.disclaimer: Inspired by publicly described methods. Not affiliated with, endorsed by, or representing Toby Crabel. Educational tool, not investment advice.

params.name: prior_days
params.doc: Previous days today's range must be narrower than (6 = NR7, 3 = NR4).

cards.name: Connors-style 2-period RSI pullback

who.text: Author of books on short-term trading, including a 2008 study written with Cesar Alvarez.

style.text: Short-term mean reversion: brief pullbacks inside long-term uptrends, measured with a 2-period RSI.

looks_for.text: Close above the 200-day simple moving average and a 2-period RSI below 10, a deep short-term oversold reading.

timeframe.text: Daily bars; trades lasting a few days.

cards.source_line: Source: Short Term Trading Strategies That Work (2008), Larry Connors and Cesar Alvarez

sources.title: Short Term Trading Strategies That Work
sources.covers: Short-term pullbacks within long-term uptrends: price above the 200-day moving average and the 2-period RSI at low (oversold) readings, with several thresholds examined.
sources.citation: Short Term Trading Strategies That Work (2008), Larry Connors and Cesar Alvarez

cards.approximation: The book examines several RSI(2) thresholds and exits; the screen lists the setup only, with the threshold editable.
cards.disclaimer: Inspired by publicly described methods. Not affiliated with, endorsed by, or representing Larry Connors and Cesar Alvarez. Educational tool, not investment advice.

cards.name: Williams-style volatility breakout

who.text: Futures trader and author of the 1999 book Long-Term Secrets to Short-Term Trading.

style.text: Short-term volatility breakouts: a move away from the day's open by part of the previous day's range.

looks_for.text: The day's high reaching the open plus a fraction (default 0.5) of the previous day's high-low range.

timeframe.text: Daily bars; very short-term trades of one to a few days.

cards.source_line: Source: Long-Term Secrets to Short-Term Trading (1999), Larry Williams

sources.title: Long-Term Secrets to Short-Term Trading
sources.covers: Short-term trading and volatility breakouts: a move from the open by a percentage of the previous day's range.
sources.citation: Long-Term Secrets to Short-Term Trading (1999), Larry Williams

cards.approximation: On end-of-day bars the screen checks the day's high; long side only; the book examines several fractions and range measures (editable here).
cards.disclaimer: Inspired by publicly described methods. Not affiliated with, endorsed by, or representing Larry Williams. Educational tool, not investment advice.

params.name: k
params.doc: Fraction of the previous day's range added to the open.
